title: The unbounded exchange extends the bounded exchange
statement:
Let $\square$ be a cartesian square of schemes [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], with $f:X\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $g:Y'\to Y$ and $g':X'\to X$. Use the derived categories of [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] and their full bounded below subcategories [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories]. Write $\iota_T:D^+(T_{\Et})\hookrightarrow D(T_{\Et})$ for the inclusions. For $K\in D^+(X_{\Et})$, the unbounded exchange $\Ex^{\mathrm{unb}}_{\square,\iota_XK}$ of [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] at coefficient ring $\mathbf Z$ equals $\iota_{Y'}(\Ex^+_{\square,K})$, where $\Ex^+$ is the exchange of [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange], under the canonical comparisons
$$u^{-1}\iota_V\cong\iota_Uu^{-1},\qquad Ru_{*,\mathrm{unb}}\iota_U\cong\iota_VRu_{*,+}\quad(u:U\to V)
$$
for the inverse images [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image] and direct images [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. These are the comparisons that compute both direct images on the same bounded below injective representative.

For any commutative ring $\Lambda$ and any sheaf $F\in\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$, place $F$ in degree zero. Under the canonical degree-zero identifications
$$
\mathcal H^0(g^{-1}Rf_*F[0])\cong g^{-1}f_*F,\qquad
\mathcal H^0(Rf'_*g'^{-1}F[0])\cong f'_*g'^{-1}F,
$$
the map $\mathcal H^0(\Ex^{\mathrm{unb},\Lambda}_{\square,F[0]})$ is the $\Lambda$-linear underived exchange. Here inverse image, direct image, and their adjunction are those on constant-ring module sheaves [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]; the underived exchange is the mate of $g'^{-1}\varepsilon_f\circ\theta_\square$ in these module categories. Its underlying abelian morphism, through the canonical coefficient comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-module-abelian-underived-exchange], is the map of [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange]. The identifications in this paragraph are induced by the augmentations into nonnegative injective resolutions. No assertion identifies the entire derived direct image of a sheaf with its ordinary direct image.

proof.text: Construct the comparison functors before comparing morphisms. Work either with abelian sheaves or with constant-ring $\Lambda$-module sheaves. The latter have enough injectives [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]. For $K\in D^+$ choose a bounded below injective complex $I$ and $K\cong QI$; $I$ is K-injective [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative]. The bounded derived direct image is represented by $Q(u_*I)$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], The functor $Q\circ C(u_*)$ on homotopy categories is triangulated: applying the additive $u_*$ to the finite direct-sum matrices defining a mapping cone gives the same cone, so cone triangles and their isomorphic copies are preserved. Every complex has a K-injective resolution [prop-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions-exist], so the unbounded one exists and has the same representative, with its right-derived comparison unit, by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived]. Comparison morphisms between K-injective representatives are unique up to homotopy and are homotopy equivalences when they represent isomorphisms [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. Applying the additive $u_*$ preserves a homotopy and a homotopy inverse (apply it to the equations defining them), so these identifications give natural comparison isomorphisms, not choices of unrelated objectwise isomorphisms. The complex $u_*I$ is still bounded below since $u_*0=0$. Inverse image is the restriction of its termwise unbounded functor [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image]. Thus all endpoints of the exchange on a bounded below input lie in $D^+$, and both right derived functors and both inverse images are compared canonically.

proof.text:
The adjunction comparison includes its unit and counit. For an edge $u$, use the exact adjunction $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] (including $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$). If $I$ is K-injective, $u_*I$ is K-injective [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective]. For every complex $M$, the canonical derived Hom bijection is computed as
$$
\operatorname{Hom}_{D(V)}(QM,Q(u_*I))
\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K(V)}(M,u_*I)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K(U)}(u^{-1}M,I)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(U)}(Q(u^{-1}M),QI).
$$
The outside arrows are [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], and the middle arrow is the inverse of the termwise adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy]. In particular the middle arrow sends $b$ to $\varepsilon_I\circ u^{-1}b$. The exact termwise inverse image is also its own left derived functor on $D$ and $D^+$ [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor]. This is the canonical derived adjunction of [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors], computed through its exact left adjoint and K-injective right-adjoint model. On bounded below representatives exactly the same three arrows compute the bounded adjunction: $D^+$ is full [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories]. The identity of $Q(u_*I)$ therefore has transpose $Q(\varepsilon_I)$ in both constructions. Likewise, if $u^{-1}M\to J$ is a K-injective replacement, the transpose of its class is represented by $M\xrightarrow{\eta_M}u_*u^{-1}M\to u_*J$. For abelian sheaves these are precisely the two characterizing properties of [prop-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-adjunction]. It follows that both units and counits coincide under the natural comparisons from step 1; this conclusion uses the displayed bijection, rather than uniqueness of right-adjoint objects without their adjunction data.

For abelian coefficients, the bounded square isomorphism is explicitly the restriction of the unbounded one, both being the localized termwise $\theta_\square$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-square-iso]. The unbounded square map used in [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] at $\mathbf Z$ is this same map. Consequently, under step 1's endpoint comparisons, its transpose is
$$
f'^{-1}g^{-1}Rf_*K\xrightarrow{\theta^D_\square}g'^{-1}f^{-1}Rf_*K\xrightarrow{g'^{-1}\varepsilon^D_{f,K}}g'^{-1}K.
$$
By step 2 the counit here is the bounded counit, so this is exactly the transpose specified in [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange]. The transpose correspondence is injective [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], hence the two exchange morphisms agree. Equivalently substitute the same $\eta_{f'}$, $\theta^D_\square$ and $\varepsilon_f$ into the explicit unit-square-counit composite in the two definitions. This proves the first clause with the comparison isomorphisms included.

proof.text:
Compute the unbounded module exchange in a form usable on a sheaf. Let $I$ be a K-injective representative of $K$ and let $j:g'^{-1}I\to J$ be a quasi-isomorphism with $J$ K-injective. The underived transpose is specified by [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange]; it is a module morphism by [lem-weil-pbc-underived-exchange-module-linear], and the module adjunction has the same unit and counit on underlying abelian sheaves by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Apply this module mate $\Ex^0$ termwise and put $e=f'_*(j)\circ\Ex^0_I:g^{-1}f_*I\to f'_*J$. The module adjunction and square maps are natural [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], [def-kun-unbounded-exchange]; the mate definition [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] consequently gives chain maps and, in the homotopy category,
$$
\varepsilon_{f',J}\circ f'^{-1}e
=j\circ\varepsilon_{f',g'^{-1}I}\circ f'^{-1}\Ex^0_I
=j\circ g'^{-1}\varepsilon_{f,I}\circ\theta_{\square,f_*I}.
$$
The first equality is naturality of the counit; the second is the defining transpose identity for the underived mate. Localize this equality. Step 2 computes the derived counit on $J$ and on $I$ by the displayed termwise counits, and [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] computes the square comparison termwise. Thus the transpose of $Q(e)$, using $Q(j)$ to identify $Q(g'^{-1}I)$ with $QJ$, is exactly the defining transpose of the unbounded exchange. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection proves that $Q(e)$ represents it. This argument works for all constant-ring module coefficients and does not assert that $g'^{-1}I$ is K-injective.

proof.text: Now let $K=F[0]$ in module sheaves. Choose nonnegative injective resolutions $s:F[0]\to I$ and $t:g'^{-1}F[0]\to J$ [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero], using enough injectives [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]; both complexes are K-injective [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative]. Exactness of $g'^{-1}$ [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] makes $g'^{-1}s$ a quasi-isomorphism: the natural comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] identifies its cohomology maps with the inverse images of the isomorphisms induced by $s$. The bijectivity for maps into $J$ in [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] gives a homotopy class $j:g'^{-1}I\to J$ whose localization is $Q(t)Q(g'^{-1}s)^{-1}$. Its composite with $g'^{-1}s$ is homotopic to $t$. In fact the equality $j\circ g'^{-1}s=t$ is strict for any representative of this class: a homotopy from a map out of $g'^{-1}F[0]$ into the nonnegative complex $J$ has its only possible component in $J^{-1}=0$. The localized $j$ is invertible, so $j$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Thus this is an allowed choice in step 4, now with augmentations whose degree-zero behavior is specified.

Naturality of the underived module mate gives
$$
\Ex^0_I\circ g^{-1}f_*s=f'_*g'^{-1}s\circ\Ex^0_F,
\qquad e\circ g^{-1}f_*s=f'_*t\circ\Ex^0_F.
$$
For completeness the naturality assertion follows by transposing the two sides of the first equality: naturality of $\theta_\square$ and $\varepsilon_f$ makes both transposes $g'^{-1}(s\circ\varepsilon_{f,F})\circ\theta_{\square,f_*F}$; the adjunction bijection is injective [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. The second equality uses $j g'^{-1}s=t$ from step 5. Since $f_*$ and $f'_*$ on modules are left exact [lem-weil-pbc-module-direct-image-left-exact], their augmentations induce the isomorphisms $f_*F\cong\mathcal H^0(f_*I)$ and $f'_*g'^{-1}F\cong\mathcal H^0(f'_*J)$ [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero]. Exactness of $g^{-1}$ [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] and the natural cohomology comparison [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] identify the first of these after $g^{-1}$ with $g^{-1}f_*F\cong\mathcal H^0(g^{-1}f_*I)$; the comparison respects the augmentation because it is induced on kernels. Taking $\mathcal H^0$ of the second displayed equality therefore identifies $\mathcal H^0(Qe)$ with $\Ex^0_F$. Step 4 identifies $Qe$ with the unbounded exchange. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-module-abelian-underived-exchange] identifies this fixed module mate, after forgetting and the specified inverse/direct-image coefficient comparisons, with [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange]. This proves precisely the degree-zero sheaf clause.
